clue.text: Extensive lack of clarity about a union fraudster

indicators.note: the two outer words are placed round the single letter of 'a', so it sits between them

parts.note: something extensive is big
mist is a lack of visual clarity

explanation.surface: A sweeping vagueness surrounding some fraud connected to a trade union or marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union, but it is a marriage: the fraudster weds more than one partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who marries while already married commits a fraud on the marriage contract, a cheat of wedlock.

clue.text: Setter ready to store ear-bone in haberdashery item

indicators.note: keeping something in store means holding it inside, so the bone goes within the other letters

parts.note: Phi is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter
the incus, or anvil, is one of the small bones of the middle ear
'on' means ready to go, as in 'you're on'

explanation.surface: The crossword setter is prepared to keep a small ear bone inside some sewing accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: Independent setters often clue themselves by pseudonym, so 'Setter' here is this puzzle's own setter; 'to store' splits that name just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stuffed pad into which pins are stuck is a staple of a haberdasher's stock.

clue.text: University probing Drosophila, mostly with success

indicators.note: something probing pushes into another thing, so the university letter goes inside
most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Drosophila is the genus name of the fruit fly

explanation.surface: A university laboratory's research on fruit flies has largely paid off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fruitful is productive, yielding good results, so it comes with success.

clue.text: Very significant couple caught hosting scam

indicators.note: a host has guests within, so the pair of letters holds the scam

parts.note: a couple is two, written as two I's (Roman numerals for one each)
a con is a scam
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A pair arrested while running a fraud is a big deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iconic is so important it becomes a symbol of its kind, hugely meaningful.

clue.text: Observed as well most of the cutting edge

parts.note: saw means observed
too means as well

indicators.note: most of the word means dropping its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone noticed, besides, the greater part of the latest innovation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting edge' looks like the latest technology but means a literal toothed blade edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated, toothed profile like that of a saw blade forms an edge that cuts.

clue.text: Fling nothing skywards — OK?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going skywards means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: FA, short for 'sweet FA', is slang for nothing
fair means OK, middling

explanation.surface: Tossing nothing up into the air: is that acceptable?
explanation.definitionFit: A brief romantic or sexual relationship is called a fling or an affair.

clue.text: Distance, not time — simple

indicators.note: not means without, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: a metre is a unit of distance

explanation.surface: It's a question of space rather than time: easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, plain, as in 'a mere child'.

clue.text: No grey rocks in beach structure

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: No grey stones in some construction on the seashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like a noun for stones on a beach, but it is a verb that scrambles NO GREY.
explanation.definitionFit: A low wall built out from the shore to check erosion is a seaside barrier against drifting sand.

clue.text: Less welcoming here in Calais leading to hesitation

parts.note: ici is French for here, as said in Calais
er is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: People are frostier over here in Calais, which makes visitors hesitate.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier means colder, and a cold reception is an unfriendly one.

clue.text: Driver getting mostly hot in Calais following twisting street there

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: chaud is French for hot
ff is the abbreviation for 'and the following' pages

indicators.note: twisting round means turning the word back to front

parts.note: rue is French for street, there meaning in Calais

explanation.surface: A driver gets quite warm in Calais after a winding road.
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to drive a private car is a chauffeur.

clue.text: Sales opportunity to the French heading for Calais — I will interrupt a great many

parts.note: au is French for 'to the'

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter
to interrupt is to break in, so the I goes inside

parts.note: tons means a great many, so a ton is a lot

explanation.surface: A chance for selling to the French on the way to Calais, if I butt in on the crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: A public sale with bidding is an opportunity to sell goods to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Attempt to host elderly drama

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the attempt holds the elderly

parts.note: a try is an attempt
aged means elderly

explanation.surface: An effort to put on a play featuring old people.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a serious play with a sad ending, one genre of theatre.

clue.text: Refurbishing topic to involve furniture item as a direct consequence

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the item goes inside the jumbled letters
refurbishing remakes something, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a sofa is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: Redecorating is a subject that brings in a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refurbishing' rearranges the five letters to IPCTO, and 'to involve' opens them after the second letter for the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'by the fact itself', used of something following automatically.

clue.text: Legislation limiting Belgium's currency

indicators.note: something limiting puts bounds around, so the legislation encloses the letter

parts.note: a rule is a piece of legislation
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A law restricting the money of Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble, also spelt with no O, is the monetary unit of Russia.

clue.text: Later course supporter of African party, say, picked up after British left

parts.note: an ANC man supports the African National Congress

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: eg (for example) means say

explanation.surface: A follower of an African political party, for instance, collected afterwards once the British departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns 'say' upside down to GE at the foot. 'Later course' is a dessert, not a later study course; the ANC is South Africa's African National Congress.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet set milk pudding served at the end of a meal is a dessert, a course that comes later.

clue.text: Tense searches producing unimportant stuff

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
rifles means rummages through, searches

explanation.surface: Someone nervously going through things comes up with nothing of value.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifles are things of little value or importance, trivial matters.

clue.text: Boss providing funds, letting secretary off for educational activity

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob or ornament

indicators.note: letting someone go, with off, means releasing them, so the secretary letters leave
off completes letting off, releasing the secretary letters from the word

parts.note: paying means providing funds
PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: A manager funding things, but letting the PA go, all for a course of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager, but it is a raised ornamental knob.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying is the act of learning from books and lessons, an educational pursuit.

clue.text: Has previously to accept one lead washer?

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the letters go inside

parts.note: hath is the old form of has
I is the Roman numeral for one
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

explanation.surface: Something has earlier taken on a single lead washer, a plumbing part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washer' suggests a plumbing ring with 'lead'; the question mark flags it as a thing to wash in.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bath in which one sits immersed to the hips is something you wash yourself in.

clue.text: Brief note following list of runners

parts.note: post means after, following
a racecard lists the runners in a race

explanation.surface: A short memo sent after the list of horses in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A short message written on a card and mailed is a brief note.

clue.text: Thing not specified in legal term offering great amusement

indicators.note: in places the unspecified thing inside the term

parts.note: Hilary term is a sitting of the English law courts (and a university term) from January
it refers to a thing not specified

explanation.surface: Something unnamed during a law sitting gives rise to much laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary is the name of a January to Easter term in English law courts and at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is boisterous merriment, great amusement and laughter.

clue.text: Even bits of this would do for workers

parts.note: the even-numbered letters of the word this are its second and fourth, joined by a conjunction to make the phrase

explanation.surface: A few parts of something here would suit some labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as the phrase 'H and S': exactly the even-numbered letters of 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands are manual labourers, as in farm workers or factory staff.

clue.text: Tribute in accepting silver

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the silver goes inside

parts.note: in means at home
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A tribute that comes in the form of silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying homage is showing honour or respect, offering a tribute.

clue.text: Change of direction in Society — we have to adopt rule

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the rule letter goes inside

parts.note: we've is the contraction of we have

explanation.surface: A shift of policy in a society, with us taking on a new regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Veering suddenly off course is a sharp change of direction.

clue.text: Possibly calumnious, nothing less, to describe a composer thus?

definitions.text: Possibly calumnious, nothing less, to describe a composer thus?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters can be rearranged into another word
less means minus, so the nothing letter is removed

parts.note: O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Calling a composer this would be slanderous, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from CALUMNIOUS and rearrange the rest; the whole clue also says that labelling a composer this way would be a slander.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking musical talent is an insult to a composer, hence calumnious.

clue.text: Made fun of Australian boor, with cut, needing care of doctor

indicators.note: being in the care of someone means being held within, so the doctor letters surround

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine, is a doctor

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an ocker is an uncultivated Australian, a boor

explanation.surface: Ridiculed an uncouth Australian with a wound, who needs medical attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The Australian slang word for a loutish man loses its tail ('with cut'), and 'needing care of' puts it in the doctor's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking someone is teasing or ridiculing them, making fun of them.

clue.text: Queen entering my hovel expressing puzzlement

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the queen letters go inside

parts.note: a sty is a filthy hovel
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch steps into my shack and is baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something baffling or inexplicable, a puzzle, causes perplexity.

clue.text: Not promising money after they turned up (from Calais, that is)

indicators.note: after places the money letter after the other letters
in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ils is French for they, the bracketed from Calais telling us to use French

explanation.surface: Not a good bet: cash after they arrived, from Calais as it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Slim chances are slender ones, offering little hope.

clue.text: Senior board member in firm about to get shock?

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
c, circa, means about
a shock is a mass of hair

explanation.surface: A top director in the company is about to receive a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks like a fright but is a thick mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shares the chairmanship of a board is one of its most senior members.

clue.text: Even cigar going out may be source of complaint

indicators.note: going out of shape or out of order suggests the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Even a cigar that keeps going out may be something to moan about.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance is a real or imagined wrong that gives grounds for complaint.

clue.text: Ridiculous figure not initially correct

indicators.note: not initially means without the first letter

parts.note: a fright is a grotesque or ridiculous-looking person

explanation.surface: An absurd-looking figure who is not, at first, quite right.
explanation.definitionFit: Right means accurate or true, the same as correct.
